name: NyayaVani Sovereign Indic Legal Knowledge Graph (GraphRAG)

nodes.act: The Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Act, 2014
nodes.title: Absolute Bar on Eviction or Confiscation Pending Survey
nodes.operative_text: No street vendor shall be evicted or relocated until the survey specified under sub-section (1) has been completed and a certificate of vending has been issued.
nodes.remedy_summary: Immediate statutory bar against administrative eviction or cart seizure.

nodes.title: Extortion & Demanding Money Under Coercion
nodes.operative_text: Whoever intentionally puts any person in fear of any injury to that person or to any other, and thereby dishonestly induces the person so put in fear to deliver to any person any property or valuable security, commits extortion.
nodes.penalty: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or with fine, or with both; Cognizable and non-bailable if aggravated.

nodes.title: Criminal Trespass & Unlawful Encroachment
nodes.operative_text: Whoever enters into or upon property in the possession of another with intent to commit an offence or to intimidate, insult or annoy any person in possession of such property commits criminal trespass.
nodes.penalty: Imprisonment up to 3 months, or fine up to ₹5,000, or both.

nodes.title: Cheating & Dishonestly Inducing Delivery of Property
nodes.operative_text: Whoever cheats and thereby dishonestly induces the person deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to make, alter or destroy the whole or any part of a valuable security, commits aggravated cheating.
nodes.penalty: Imprisonment up to 7 years and mandatory fine; Cognizable.

nodes.title: Punishment for Cheating by Personation by Using Computer Resource
nodes.operative_text: Whoever, by means of any communication device or computer resource cheats by personating, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to one lakh rupees.
nodes.remedy_summary: Immediate blocking of digital lending app and freezing of offending UPI accounts via cybercrime.gov.in.

nodes.title: Prohibition of Harassment & Direct Account Disbursement
nodes.operative_text: Lending service providers (LSPs) and Regulated Entities (REs) are strictly prohibited from accessing borrower phone contacts, photos, or media. Harassment by recovery agents invokes cancellation of RE lending license.
nodes.remedy_summary: Direct regulatory complaint to RBI Banking Ombudsman (cms.rbi.org.in).

nodes.title: Causing Death or Grievous Injury by Rash and Negligent Act
nodes.operative_text: Whoever causes the death of any person by doing any rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine.
nodes.penalty: Imprisonment up to 5 years (up to 10 years for failure to report in hit-and-run).

nodes.title: Application for Compensation before Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (MACT)
nodes.operative_text: An application for compensation arising out of an accident involving death of or bodily injury to persons, or damage to any property of a third party, may be made by the victim or legal representatives before the MACT within six months.
nodes.remedy_summary: Statutory Third-Party insurance claim payout covering medical expenses, income loss, and pain and suffering.

nodes.title: Duty of Driver in Case of Accident and Injury
nodes.operative_text: The driver of the motor vehicle shall take all reasonable steps to secure medical attention for the injured person and report the accident to the nearest police station within twenty-four hours.
nodes.remedy_summary: Mandatory compliance step preserving insurance indemnity and avoiding criminal liability.

nodes.title: Return of Amount and Compensation for Delayed Possession
nodes.operative_text: If the promoter fails to complete or is unable to give possession of an apartment in accordance with the terms of the agreement for sale, the promoter shall be liable on demand to the allottees to return the amount received with interest at SBI highest marginal lending rate plus 2%.
nodes.remedy_summary: Right to claim 100% refund with SBI MCLR + 2% compound interest or monthly delay interest until handover.

nodes.act: Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006 (MSMED)
nodes.title: Mandatory 45-Day Payment & Compound Interest at Three Times RBI Rate
nodes.operative_text: Where any buyer buys any goods or services from a micro or small enterprise, the buyer shall make payment on or before the agreed date, not exceeding forty-five days. If defaulted, the buyer is liable to pay compound interest with monthly rests at three times the bank rate notified by the Reserve Bank.
nodes.remedy_summary: Statutory right to 3x RBI compound interest with monthly rests; non-tax-deductible for the defaulting buyer.

nodes.title: Claims Arising Out of Deductions from Wages or Delay in Payment
nodes.operative_text: Application may be presented to the Authority appointed by the State Government for direction to pay delayed wages along with compensation up to ten times the amount deducted.
nodes.remedy_summary: Labor commissioner order for release of unpaid wages plus up to 10x penalty.

nodes.title: Mandatory Registration of First Information Report (Zero FIR)
nodes.operative_text: Every information relating to the commission of a cognizable offence shall be recorded in writing by the officer in charge of a police station, irrespective of the area where the offence was committed (Zero FIR), and transferred to the jurisdictional station.
nodes.remedy_summary: Police station cannot turn away victim citing jurisdictional boundaries; registration is statutorily mandatory.

nodes.title: Escalation to Superintendent of Police upon Refusal by Station Officer
nodes.operative_text: Any person aggrieved by a refusal on the part of an officer in charge of a police station to record the information may send the substance of such information, in writing and by post, to the Superintendent of Police concerned.
nodes.remedy_summary: Direct registered post statutory escalation compelling investigation.

nodes.title: Fundamental Right to Practice Any Profession, Trade or Business
nodes.operative_text: All citizens shall have the right to practise any profession, or to carry on any occupation, trade or business, subject only to reasonable statutory regulation in the interest of the general public.
nodes.remedy_summary: Constitutional shield invalidating arbitrary administrative clampdowns on lawful vendors.

nodes.title: Right to Life Encompassing the Right to Livelihood and Shelter
nodes.operative_text: No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law. The Supreme Court in Olga Tellis held that the right to life includes the right to livelihood, which cannot be extinguished without fair procedure and rehabilitation.
nodes.remedy_summary: Supreme Court doctrine prohibiting summary demolition without reasonable notice and rehabilitation.

nodes.title: Freedom of Conscience and Free Profession, Practice and Propagation of Religion
nodes.operative_text: Subject to public order, morality and health, all persons are equally entitled to freedom of conscience and the right freely to profess, practise and propagate religion.
nodes.remedy_summary: Absolute constitutional defense against vigilante or mob interference in lawful religious worship.

nodes.title: Admissibility of Electronic Records & Cryptographic Verification
nodes.operative_text: Any information contained in an electronic record which is printed on a paper, stored, recorded or copied in optical or magnetic media shall be deemed to be also a document and shall be admissible in any proceedings, provided conditions of integrity, custody and contemporaneous recording are certified.
nodes.remedy_summary: Cryptographically hashed contemporaneous voice recording is prima facie admissible evidence in Indian courts.

nodes.act: Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 & BNS Section 274/275
nodes.title: Prohibition of Adulterated, Contaminated or Noxious Food Sale & Lawful Police Seizure
nodes.operative_text: No person shall manufacture, store, sell or distribute any food article which is unsafe, misbranded or contains foreign matter harmful to health. Food Safety Officers and police have statutory authority to inspect premises, seize contaminated stock, cancel licenses, and register criminal proceedings under BNS Section 274.
nodes.remedy_summary: Citizen is legally at fault. Police and Food Safety authorities are acting lawfully to protect public health. The citizen has no right to challenge lawful confiscation of hazardous goods.

nodes.title: Drunk Driving, Helmetless Riding, Dangerous Driving & Lawful Impoundment
nodes.operative_text: Driving with blood alcohol exceeding 30mg per 100ml or driving dangerously on the wrong side constitutes a cognizable offense punishable with fine up to ₹10,000 and imprisonment. Under Section 207, any police officer in uniform is statutorily authorized to seize and detain the vehicle until compounded.
nodes.remedy_summary: Citizen is legally at fault. Traffic police are exercising lawful statutory powers under MV Act Section 207. Citizen must pay statutory compounding fine and cannot dispute lawful seizure.

nodes.act: Street Vendors Act, 2014 & Municipal Corporation Act
nodes.section: Section 3(2) Street Vendors Act & Section 314 Municipal Act
nodes.title: Prohibition of Permanent Footpath Structures & Blocking Emergency Facilities
nodes.operative_text: No street vendor or shopkeeper shall carry out vending or construct any permanent brick, mortar, or iron structure on a footpath, pedestrian walkway, or within 50 meters of a hospital emergency gate, railway station entry, or fire station. Municipal authorities have lawful authority to dismantle and remove such obstruction immediately without notice.
nodes.remedy_summary: Citizen is legally at fault. Erecting permanent obstructions or blocking emergency zones is expressly excluded from Street Vendors Act protections under Section 3(2). Municipal clearance is lawful.

nodes.title: Lawful Enforcement of Security Interest for Non-Performing Assets (NPA)
nodes.operative_text: When any borrower, who is under a liability to a secured creditor, makes any default in repayment of secured debt and his account is classified as non-performing asset (NPA) after 90 days, the secured creditor may require the borrower by notice in writing to discharge in full his liabilities within sixty days, failing which the bank has lawful right to take possession of the secured assets.
nodes.remedy_summary: Bank is acting lawfully. A formal 60-day demand notice under SARFAESI Section 13(2) is a valid statutory enforcement procedure. The borrower must either cure the default or file an appeal before the DRT under Section 17.

edges.meaning: Street vending protection draws constitutional authority from Article 19(1)(g).
Official demanding money or threatening confiscation commits criminal extortion under BNS Section 308.
Vendor's voice statement and video of seizure preserved as admissible electronic evidence under BSA Section 63.
Digital loan app extortion and contact morphing constitute aggravated fraud under BNS Section 318(4).
Violates mandatory RBI digital lending regulations banning access to contacts and harassment.
Cyber extortion is a cognizable cybercrime requiring immediate Zero FIR and cybercrime portal dispatch.
Unlawful demolition or encroachment without court decree constitutes criminal trespass.
Disruption of peaceful religious assembly mandates immediate Zero FIR registration by police.
If police station refuses Zero FIR, mandatory escalation to Superintendent of Police via registered post.
Third-party collision claim co-exists with criminal prosecution of offending driver under BNS Section 106.
Driver and victim must adhere to statutory 24-hour First Accident Report (FAR) intimation.
Dashcam footage, roadside voice intake, and vehicle damage logs preserved under BSA Section 63.
Invoice delivery receipts, work orders, and email trails hashed for Samadhaan Council arbitration.
Unlawful denial of earned wages deprives worker of constitutional right to livelihood under Article 21.
